annotationRationale: The main method counts the multiples directly and again through their contributions to the sets. Divisibility and the spacing of multiples support both routes. Units-digit congruences and addition across disjoint cases are specific to the alternative.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate for this finite counting problem; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Each ten-number block contains one or two multiples of 7. There are 142 multiples from 1 through 1000, so exactly 142−100=42 blocks contain two, agreeing with choice B. The stem, choices and key are consistent; there are no figures or grading exceptions.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2022_AMC_10B_Q08/count-the-extra-multiples and 2022_AMC_10B_Q08/locate-the-first-multiple are both retained and independently verified for the identical partition and choices. AoPS Solution 1 matches the retained position route. Its seven-block pattern is an equivalent periodic organization of those residue classes, so another route is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: Double counting is correctly assessed for the main solution, with factors and multiples as support. Congruences and disjoint-case addition correctly appear only in the alternative method.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate for this finite counting problem; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Seven consecutive integers guarantee a multiple. Three multiples span at least 14, exceeding a block's endpoint difference of 9, so every block contains exactly one or two. The endpoint calculation gives 142 multiples, and 2t+(100−t)=142 correctly yields t=42.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly reuses 2022_AMC_10B_Q08#count-the-extra-multiples, retaining randommath-reference-2022_AMC_10B_Q08. The current LIVE explanation and AoPS Solution 3 corroborate the route. The project reuse and third-party basis are honestly identified as source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The crucial one-or-two restriction is proved, and the partition explains why each multiple contributes exactly once to the equation. The total and both endpoint inequalities are explicit.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:double-counting precisely captures counting the same multiples directly and by blocks. cnm_p153 supports divisibility and spacing of multiples.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The accepted factors-and-multiples link supplies genuine elementary support, extended beyond its stated small-number scope. Double counting has no supplied CN link.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: Supporting multiple recognition overlaps 4.OA.B.4, but counting through 1000 extends beyond that standard's 1–100 scope. Double counting has no supplied US alignment, and this solution does not cover the standard's other requirements.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: Both immediate nodes are directly supported. The assessed/support distinction correctly identifies double counting as the main reasoning.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The span argument forces two multiples in a block to be consecutive, with the earlier in position 1, 2 or 3. The corresponding earlier multiples are exactly 21+70j, 42+70j and 63+70j. Their last included values are 931, 952 and 973; their next values exceed 1000. Thus each class has 14 entries, and the one-to-one correspondence with qualifying blocks gives 42.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly reuses 2022_AMC_10B_Q08#locate-the-first-multiple and retains its inherited live-reference-2022_AMC_10B_Q08 credit. The supplied current AoPS Solution 1 independently corroborates the position classification. The project method's underlying provenance is preserved without an official-MAA claim.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: Necessity and sufficiency of the first-three-positions condition are explained. The initial values, period 70, index endpoints and absence of double counting are justified, making all three case totals reconstructible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_p153 supports multiples and common periods; math:modular-congruence matches units-digit classes; cnm_h230 matches addition across the three mutually exclusive cases.
